docs.html:
1Purpose

This policy sets out what [Provider name] commits to when we provide . It is for whose situation carries high risk or complexity, their families and advocates, our , and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every participant who receives specialised support coordination from [Provider name], and every person who asks us for it, before they sign (the Registration Rules, Schedule 6, clause 1(2)(a)).
  • Everyone who works for us on that support: employees, contractors, agency workers, volunteers and key personnel.
  • The whole of the coordination: assessing , planning for a , finding and briefing , monitoring, and reporting.
  • Any other support we or anyone connected with us provide to the same participant. Commitment 13 keeps it separate from the coordination.

Short names used here:

  • "The Registration Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018.
  • "The Incident Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.
  • "The Code" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018, section 6.

3Commitments

C1

We will allocate each participant a coordinator who is qualified, trained and signed off as competent for that participant's risks and complexity. A coordinator holds [qualification and years of experience we require]. The expects specialised support coordination to be delivered by a qualified and experienced practitioner, such as a social worker, psychologist, occupational therapist or mental health nurse, or a person with equivalent demonstrated experience in complex situations; set the requirement at adoption with that in mind. They have completed our training on the risk factors listed in FRM-SCO-01 . They have supervision with the Service Manager at least every month.

C2

We will assess each participant's risks and complexity with them. We use their own account and the risk factors and rating scale in FRM-SCO-01 Risk and Crisis Response Plan. At the first meeting we agree interim safety steps and set a provisional risk level. We make the plan within the time for that level in PRO-SCO-02 Decision table 2, counted from the first meeting: 5 for extreme risk, 10 for high, 15 for medium and low. A second person, the , reads and challenges the assessment and plan: before the plan is issued for a participant at high or extreme risk, and within 10 business days of issue for every other participant.

C3

We will make a Risk and Crisis Response Plan with each participant, in their words and in a form they can use. It names their warning signs, what helps, and who does what if a crisis or a happens. We give the participant their copy. We review the plan at the interval for their risk level, and after any crisis, incident or major change.

C4

We will always have someone who has read the participant's plan and can respond to a crisis. That is the coordinator, or the when the coordinator is away. In our hours a coordinator or cover who has read the plan answers a crisis call and starts the plan within 2 hours. Outside our hours the participant's plan names who they call, and we say truthfully whether that is us.

C5

We will consult the participant when we plan and coordinate supports, and before each plan review. With their consent, we also consult their and . We record who the participant agreed we may talk to and what we may tell them. We respect a refusal.

C6

We will identify suitable providers for each support. We check registration where it applies, evidence of skills and experience for the participant's kind of situation, and fit with their preferences. We follow one rule, set in POL-SCO-02 C4: at least three suitable options able to meet the need, of which at least two have no relationship to us, where that many exist, and we say which have a relationship to us. Where fewer exist we record who we asked and tell the participant why.

C7

We will make sure every provider who carries out the plan understands the participant's risks and their own part before their first support. We brief each provider on the parts of the plan the participant agreed to share. We get their confirmation in writing.

C8

We will bring the participant's providers and other services together to work as one team. We hold a coordination meeting at the interval for the participant's risk level. We hold another within 5 business days after any crisis, incident or breakdown of supports. Every action has an owner and a date.

C9

We will monitor each participant's plan. We contact the participant at the interval for their risk level and check that each support is delivered as planned. When a support is not delivered as planned we act within 5 business days.

C10

We will check each participant's plan budget and plan dates every month, in the first 5 business days of the month. For each funding category we compare the share used and booked with the share of plan time elapsed. A gap of more than 15 percentage points is explained, and the participant is told within 5 business days, and their too if they have one. This is the same monthly as POL-SCO-02 C11. It is done once, under PRO-SCO-02 step 22, and recorded on FRM-SCO-02 Section H. When a plan is within 12 weeks of its reassessment date and no review has been scheduled, we ask the NDIA to confirm one.

C11

We will meet every reporting obligation attached to the participant's plan. We list each report and notice owed when coordination starts: the NDIA's implementation report, due 8 weeks after coordination starts; mid-term reports at the frequency the request for service sets; and the plan reassessment report before the plan review, which we draft with the participant 8 weeks before the reassessment date and send 6 weeks before it, or by the date the NDIA sets. Due dates come from the request for service and the provider portal. We show the participant each report about them before we send it. We send it by its due date, or tell the recipient before the date passes if we will miss it.

C12

We will arrange supports as the participant directs, using their plan for the purposes they intend. We give them their options in the language and form they understand, and build their skills to manage their own supports if they wish. POL-SCO-02 Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Policy sets this out.

C13

We will keep specialised support coordination separate from any other support we, or anyone connected with us, provide. We give each participant our conflict of policy and its plain summary in the format they use, and check they can say back what it means. We explain, and check they can say back, how coordination differs from the other supports in their plan. We take no payment, gift or benefit for naming or referring a provider. We tell the participant about any interest we hold before they choose, and their choice of provider never changes their coordination. We record every referral to or from another provider in REG-SCO-02 Support Coordination Referral Register. PRO-SCO-01 Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Procedure sets how.

C14

We will not leave a participant without a plan when coordination ends or changes. Before our last day we hand the Risk and Crisis Response Plan to the next coordinator, with the participant's consent. We also give the participant their copy.

4Ground rules

G1

The participant leads. Their words, their choices and their pace come first. We never decide for a participant who can decide for themselves.

G2

We share a participant's information only with the people they have agreed to. The exceptions are a call to 000, a legal duty, and a serious threat to life, health or safety when we cannot ask first. We tell the participant at the start that these exceptions exist, and tell them if we use one.

G3

A coordinator is not a clinician or a behaviour support practitioner. We pass health and behaviour questions to the participant's practitioner. We never write a restrictive practice into a plan. Only an authorised behaviour support plan can hold one. PRO-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Procedure applies if someone asks.

G4

A participant who says no has made a decision. We record it, ask again at the next review, and never end coordination because of it.

G5

We say our hours truthfully. We do not suggest we are a crisis service unless we staff one. The participant's plan says who they call outside our hours.

G6

Nobody at [Provider name] can extend a time limit that the law sets.

G7

A participant at high or extreme risk never goes without interim safety steps, a cover coordinator and a named person to call.

G8

A concern about a coordinator goes to the Service Manager. A concern about the Service Manager goes to the Chief Executive. A concern about the Chief Executive goes to the chair of the governing body. In a provider with one owner it goes to the . Anyone can also phone the on 1800 035 544.

G9

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader holds every role except the case reviewer, who is a person outside the business. The cover coordinator may be a coordinator from another provider, engaged in writing. The independent contact for concerns may be the case reviewer. The case reviewer also gives the sole trader supervision at least every month, reads the register as REG-SCO-01 sets out, and does the checks in "How we check" that would otherwise be the sole trader checking their own work. The sole trader engages the case reviewer and any outside cover in writing, with a confidentiality undertaking and agreed response times, names them on adoption and tells each participant who they are.

G10

The system does not depend on any one software product. Paper works when systems are down.

G11

Every participant is told how to complain, and how to change their coordinator or a provider. We tell them at the first meeting and at each plan review. POL-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Policy sets how we handle a complaint.

7Authority

411 words
  • NDIS Practice Standards, Module 4, Specialised Support Coordination: Quality Indicators Guidelines section 64; Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 6, clause 3.
  • The same Module, sections 65 and 66 and Schedule 6, clauses 4 and 5, which POL-SCO-02 and PRO-SCO-01 answer in full. POL-SCO-02 is the controlled policy for clause 4; commitment 12 is a pointer to it. Commitment 13 carries the clause 5 commitments, and PRO-SCO-01 sets the steps.
  • The Registration Rules, section 20(3), the item for specialised support coordination: it is assessed against Schedules 1 and 6, by certification.
  • The Registration Rules, Schedule 1, clauses 3, 6, 12, 15, 16, 19 and 22. They cover person-centred supports, informed choice, information, workers, continuity, support planning and transitions.
  • The Registration Rules, section 7: the classes of supports that need a registered provider.
  • NDIS Act 2013, section 73B (note): where the NDIA manages the funds, only a registered provider may give the support.
  • NDIS Act 2013, section 73ZDA: the NDIS Provider Register, which lists registered providers, their classes of supports, conditions and suspensions, and banning orders.
  • NDIS Act 2013, sections 73F(2)(b), (c), (g) and (h) and 73J. Complying with the Code, the Practice Standards and the incident rules is a condition of registration.
  • The Code, section 6(1)(a) to (g). It covers respect for self-determination, privacy, safe and competent supports, integrity, raising concerns, and preventing violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation and sexual misconduct.
  • The Incident Rules: Part 2, sections 9, 10 and 12, and Part 3, sections 19, 20, 21 and 25.
  • National Disability Insurance Scheme (Approved Quality Auditors Scheme) Guidelines 2018, Annex B, items B.2 and B.3. Specialised support coordination is a high risk group for audit sampling. Participants are in the sample unless they opt out.
  • The NDIS Pricing Arrangements and Price Limits, for the conditions and that apply to specialised support coordination.
  • Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), where it applies to us, and the privacy and health records law of [state or territory].
  • The child protection, guardianship, mental health and criminal law of [state or territory].
  • Law changing: from 20 November 2026 a new section 73VA of the NDIS Act 2013 makes it an offence and a civil penalty for an NDIS provider to give or offer any gift or benefit likely to induce a person to use its services. It comes from Act No. 66, 2026, Schedule 2, Part 8. Our rule in commitment 13 is wider and already covers it. Review commitment 13 and PRO-SCO-02 step 14 before that date.

9Words we use

471 words
specialised support coordination
help for a participant whose situation carries high risk or complexity. It means putting their NDIS plan into action, monitoring it and reviewing it, and reducing the risk and complexity of their situation.
participant
a person with disability who receives specialised support coordination from us, or who is asking us for it.
NDIS plan
the plan the NDIA approves for the participant, with its funding and dates.
NDIA
the National Disability Insurance Agency, which runs the NDIS and approves NDIS plans. The Quality Indicators call it "the Agency".
coordinator
the worker who does the coordination with a participant.
cover coordinator
a second coordinator, with the same sign-off, who acts when the coordinator is away. For a sole trader this may be a coordinator from another provider, engaged in writing.
case reviewer
a person who reads the assessment and plan for each participant, and challenges them. They are not the coordinator for that participant. For a sole trader the case reviewer is a person outside the business.
Risk and Crisis Response Plan
the plan we make with the participant in FRM-SCO-01. It holds their risks, warning signs, what helps and the steps to take in a crisis.
risk and complexity
the things in a participant's life that could seriously harm them or others. It also means anything that makes their supports hard to arrange or keep steady.
crisis
a point where someone is at risk of serious harm, or where supports the participant depends on have broken down or are about to.
breakdown of supports
a support the participant relies on stops, or is not delivered as planned, and the participant is at risk or worse off.
critical support
a support that would put the participant at risk if it stopped, named in FRM-SCO-01 Risk and Crisis Response Plan.
provider
an NDIS provider, registered or not, who gives a support in the participant's NDIS plan.
mainstream service
a service for the whole community, such as health, housing, justice, child safety, mental health, education or transport.
support network
the people in the participant's life whom they choose to involve, such as family, friends, carers and advocates.
independent advocate
a person outside [Provider name] who speaks up for the participant's wishes and rights.
decision maker
a person with legal authority to make decisions for a participant, such as a guardian, administrator or nominee.
interest
ownership of a provider, a shared owner or director, a family tie, a referral arrangement, or any payment, gift or benefit from a provider.
independent contact for concerns
in a provider with one owner, the outside person who receives concerns about the owner. REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register names them. This may be the case reviewer.
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

This policy sets out how [Provider name] makes sure each directs how their NDIS are used, and gets good value from them. It is for participants, their families and advocates, our , and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Everyone who works for [Provider name] on : employees, contractors, agency workers, volunteers and key personnel.
  • Every participant who receives specialised support coordination from us, whoever manages their funds: the , a or the participant.
  • Every decision about how a participant's funds are used, from choosing a to changing or ending a support.

Short names used here:

  • "The Practice Standards Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018.
  • "The Code Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018.

4Ground rules

G1

The participant decides. A family member, worker, provider or plan manager may advise but never decides for them. Where a law gives another person the decision, commitment 2 applies.

G2

We give our own view only when the participant asks for it. We say it is our view, and we never present it as the only choice.

G3

We refuse every gift, payment or benefit from a provider. We record every offer on FRM-GOV-01 Conflict of Declaration Form the same day.

G4

We share a participant's information with a provider, service or person only as the participant agreed in FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form. We share only what the task needs.

G5

We never guess what the plan covers. Where the plan is unclear we help the participant ask their NDIA contact or planner, with their consent, and we tell the participant what was asked and what was answered.

G6

For NDIA-managed and plan-managed funds, a price above the NDIA cannot be claimed, so we tell the participant and offer other options. A self-managed participant may agree a higher price: we tell them the limit, what the difference will cost from their budget, and record their decision. Where no limit applies, we compare the price with similar options and record it.

G7

A participant may ask for more time at any step. We give it, and we tell them of any real deadline and where it comes from. No time limit in PRO-SCO-03 shortens their time to decide.

G8

A change to a decision is a new record. The old record stays as it was, and the new one gives the reason.

G9

A coordinator works alone only after they have walked through PRO-SCO-03 with the Service Manager. REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register records it.

G10

Where we also provide other supports to the same participant, POL-SCO-01 Specialised Support Coordination Policy applies. It sets how we keep coordination separate and tell the participant about our interest.

G11

In a small provider one person may hold several roles, such as coordinator, Service Manager and Quality Manager. For a sole trader the , a person outside the business named on adoption (POL-SCO-01 ground rule 9), does each check in "How we check" that would otherwise be someone checking their own work. They read five records every 3 months, or all of them if we have fewer than five. REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register names the , who receives concerns about the owner and may be the same person.

G12

A worker with a concern about a colleague or a manager raises it with the Chief Executive. A concern about the Chief Executive or the owner goes to the chair of the governing body or the independent contact for concerns. POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy protects the worker.

7Authority

486 words
  • NDIS Practice Standards, Module 4, Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports: Quality Indicators Guidelines section 65; Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 6, clause 4. This is the controlled policy for clause 4; POL-SCO-01 commitment 12 points here.
  • Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 6, clauses 3 and 5: specialised support coordination and conflict of interest, the standards that sit beside this one.
  • Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 1, clauses 3, 4, 6, 12, 13 and 20: person-centred supports, individual values and beliefs, independence and informed choice, information management, complaints and service agreements.
  • NDIS Act 2013, sections 73F(2)(b) and (c), 73J, 73T and 73V: complying with the NDIS Code of Conduct and the Practice Standards is a condition of registration.
  • NDIS Act 2013, section 73B (note) and section 73ZDA: when the NDIA manages the funds, a registered provider must provide the supports. The NDIS Provider Register lists registered providers and banning orders.
  • Code Rules, section 6(1)(a), (b), (d), (e) and (f): self-determination and decision-making, privacy, integrity, honesty and transparency, raising concerns, and preventing exploitation.
  • National Disability Insurance Scheme (Complaints Management and Resolution) Rules 2018, when a participant complains about our advice or a decision.
  • NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years. That is the floor for every record of a support we arranged or claimed. Seven years is our standard for the other records in this thread, and until the participant turns 25 where they were under 18. It matches the 7 years the Incident Rules and the Complaints Rules set for their records.
  • Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), where it applies to us, and the privacy and health records law of [state or territory].
  • The guardianship and decision-making law of [state or territory]: who may decide for a participant.
  • Law changing: from 20 November 2026 a new section 73VA of the NDIS Act 2013 makes it an offence and a civil penalty for an NDIS provider to give or offer any gift or benefit likely to induce a person to use its services (Act No. 66, 2026, Schedule 2, Part 8). Ground rule 3 already bars gifts and benefits. Review it on that date.
  • Law changing: from 1 December 2026 the time a provider has to make a payment claim under the NDIS Act 2013 falls. It is 2 years now and becomes 90 days. Review step 26 of PRO-SCO-03 on that date.
  • Law changing: from 1 February 2027 the Act's rules on plan renewal and on reasonable and necessary supports change. Review commitment 9 and steps 6, 24 and 30 of PRO-SCO-03 before that date.
  • Law changing: the Act will require plan managers to be registered, on a date to be fixed. When it starts, a registered plan manager cannot also be registered for other supports: remove plan management from our list of interests or restructure. Review how we record the plan manager (FRM-SCO-02 Q5) when it starts.

value for money
the best result for the participant's goals from the funds, judged on price and quality together, not on price alone.
skills plan
the small steps a participant agrees to take to coordinate, direct or manage more of their own supports.
funds check
our monthly comparison, for each funding category, of the share of the participant's funds used and booked with the share of plan time elapsed.
independent contact for concerns
in a small provider, the outside person who receives concerns about the owner. This may be the case reviewer.
case reviewer
the person who reads and challenges coordination work, as POL-SCO-01 sets out. For a sole trader, a person outside the business who also does the checks that would otherwise be done by the person who did the work.

a person or business that pays a participant's providers from their funds and keeps the records for them.

the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission, which registers and oversees providers.
independent advocate
a person outside [Provider name] who speaks up for the participant's wishes and rights.
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.
price limit
the most that can be claimed from NDIA-managed or plan-managed funds for a type of support, set by the NDIA. A self-managed participant may agree a higher price. Where none applies to a support, we say so on the record.

1Purpose

The result: each decides how their are used, understands their , builds the skills they want, and sees their funds used well.

This procedure gives effect to POL-SCO-02 Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Policy, C1 to C14.

Short names used here:

  • "The " means the National Disability Insurance Agency. The Quality Indicators call it "the Agency".
  • "Funds" means the NDIS amounts in the participant's plan.
  • "The Code Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018.

2When and who

Start this procedure when any of these happens:

  • a participant starts with us
  • a participant asks for a new support, or to change or end one
  • a participant says a support is not working
  • a , a 3 monthly review or a plan review comes due.

Who acts:

  • The does every step.
  • The Service Manager takes every escalation, and names a for each participant (PRO-SCO-02 step 1).
  • The Quality Manager samples the records. POL-SCO-02 sets those checks, so they are not steps here.

If you are a sole trader, you do every step yourself. Where a step says to tell the Service Manager, write the date and time and, for a participant at high or extreme risk or for a same-day matter, tell your : the person outside the business named on adoption (PRO-SCO-02, When and who). The case reviewer reads five of your records every 3 months, or all of them if you have fewer than five. A concern about you goes to the named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register; this may be the case reviewer.

3Before you start

  • You have a new copy of FRM-SCO-02 Support Options and Choice Record for this decision, funds check or review. It has its own record number.
  • You know where the participant's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form and FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form are filed.
  • You have time booked with the participant. They choose the place, the time and who comes.
  • You have walked through this procedure with the Service Manager. REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register shows it.
  • For a funds check, you have the figures from the participant, the or the NDIA portal, with consent.

Before first use, the Service Manager checks that this procedure has no square bracket left to fill. The cover coordinator for each participant is named under PRO-SCO-02 step 1. The Quality Manager checks that none is left blank.

Urgent path: where the support is critical or urgent (PRO-SCO-02 step 15; PRO-SCO-01 Decision table 3), do steps 5 to 20 within 3 , by phone where needed, and complete the record within 2 business days afterwards. The participant still chooses. The urgent path shortens our clocks, never their time to decide; you tell them plainly what will stop and when.

4Watch out

  • The participant decides, not the person pushing. A family member, or worker may press for a choice. Following them instead of the participant takes away the participant's control. It can also hide abuse or exploitation.
  • "Do you understand?" is not a check. People say yes to end a hard conversation. A choice made without understanding is not the participant's choice.
  • Never hold their money. We are not the participant's plan manager. Money that passes through us is unlawful plan management and a conflict of , and it can harm the participant.
  • Never take a gift or benefit from a provider. It makes your advice untrue. It is a conflict of interest and may be a breach of the Code Rules.
  • A guess is not a "no". Telling a participant their plan will not cover something, without checking, can stop them using funds they are entitled to.
  • Share only what the participant agreed. Telling a provider more than they agreed breaches their privacy.
  • A rushed choice is not a free choice. Pressure to decide fast, or a false deadline, leaves the participant with a support they did not choose.
  • Funds can run out or sit unused without anyone noticing. A support that stops partway through a plan can leave the participant without care.
  • Our interest must be known before they choose. If we, or someone linked to us, gain from an option, the participant must hear it from us first.

Start with the participant. An adult decides for themself unless a legal document says otherwise. Use Decision table 1. Ask to see any guardianship order, nomination or parental authority, note what it covers and when it ends, and file a copy. Write the record number in question 1.

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 1POL-SCO-02 C1Written on: →Form, question 7Form Q7→Form, question 8Form Q8

Step 6

Warning. Telling a participant "the plan will not cover that" on a guess can stop them using funds they are entitled to.

Coordinator

Check whether the support can be arranged as the participant wants.

Use Decision table 2. Check the plan wording, the support category, the NDIA that applies and how the funds are managed, and whether the support is safe and lawful. If you are not sure, help the participant ask their NDIA contact or planner, with their consent, and record the question and the date. Step 7's time runs from the answer, and you tell the participant what is waiting. Do not guess.

Result
You know whether you can arrange it, and why.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q9
Time limit
Within 5 business days of step 5 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 7POL-SCO-02 C7Written on: →Form, question 9Form Q9

Step 7

Coordinator

If you cannot arrange the support as the participant wants:

Tell the participant what you cannot do, why, and what else is possible.

Use their way of communicating. Offer the nearest option, other funds if the plan allows, a request to the NDIA to change the plan, and an . Tell them how to complain, as PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure sets out. Help them ask for a review if they want one. The NDIA decision notice says how and by when. Do not decide for them. When they choose, carry on from step 8 with the changed need. If the reason is that the support is unlawful, tell the Service Manager the same day.

Result
The participant knows where they stand and chooses what to do next.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q10
Time limit
Within 2 business days of step 6 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 7POL-SCO-02 C7Written on: →Form, question 10Form Q10

Options

Step 8

Coordinator

Find the options for each need.

Follow the options rule in POL-SCO-02 C4: find at least three suitable options able to meet the need, of which at least two have no relationship to us, where that many exist, and say which have a relationship to us (step 12). List , community groups and such as family and friends as well, not instead. Add every provider the participant names. Never leave one out because it competes with us, or because you do not know it. If fewer exist, write why.

Result
A fair list of options exists, and it is not limited to what we know or sell.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q11
Time limit
Within 10 business days of step 6 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 4POL-SCO-02 C4←POL-SCO-02, commitment 13POL-SCO-02 C13Written on: →Form, question 11Form Q11

Step 9

Warning. A provider that is not registered cannot be paid from NDIA-managed funds. A provider whose banning order covers this support must never be put to a participant.

Coordinator

Check each funded provider on the NDIS Provider Register.

Check that the provider is registered for this support. Check for a banning order and read what it prohibits or restricts. Note the date. Drop any provider whose order covers this support, and tell the Service Manager. If the funds are NDIA-managed, drop any provider that is not registered, and tell the participant why. For other funds, tell the participant that an unregistered provider is not assessed against the NDIS Practice Standards. The Code of Conduct still applies to them.

Result
Every funded option can be paid from the participant's funds, and none is banned.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q12
Time limit
Before step 13 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 4POL-SCO-02 C4Written on: →Form, question 12Form Q12

Step 10

Coordinator

Ask each provider and service the same questions, and write the answers.

Ask the same questions of every option. Ask what the support would do, the price for each unit and the total for what the participant wants. Ask how soon it can start, where, and who would deliver it. Ask how the participant can change or end it. Ask only what you need. Name the participant only with their consent. Write "not known" where you could not find out.

Result
Every option has the same facts, so the participant can compare them.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q13
Time limit
Within 10 business days of step 6 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 4POL-SCO-02 C4Written on: →Form, question 13Form Q13

Step 11

Coordinator

Compare the options on price and quality against what the participant wants.

Check how the funds for this support are managed. For NDIA-managed and plan-managed funds, a price above the NDIA price limit cannot be claimed: tell the participant and offer other options. For self-managed funds the participant may pay more: tell them the limit, what the difference will cost from their budget, and record their decision. Where no limit applies, compare the price with similar options and write that. Compare the total with the funds left. Compare quality on what matters to the participant: skills, experience, place, hours, culture and language. Do not rank by cost alone. Keep a dearer option on the list if the participant may prefer it.

Result
The participant has a plain comparison tied to their own goals.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q14
Time limit
Before step 13 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 4POL-SCO-02 C4Written on: →Form, question 14Form Q14

Step 12

Coordinator

If we, or a person or business linked to us, provide an option or gain from it:

Tell the participant about the interest before they hear about the option.

Follow PRO-SCO-01 Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Procedure and complete FRM-SCO-03 Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Disclosure Record. Show the option as one among the others. Tell the participant that their choice will not change how we coordinate for them.

Result
The participant knows of our interest before they hear about the option.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q15
Time limit
Before step 13 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 4POL-SCO-02 C4Written on: →Form, question 15Form Q15

Step 13

Coordinator

Go through the options with the participant, one at a time, in the format they use.

Prepare each option in their format before you meet: spoken, large print, pictures or symbols, a plain summary, audio or video, a translation, or Auslan. Let them set the pace and the place. Say what each option would do, cost and need, and how soon it could start. Say what you do not know. Give your own view only if they ask, and say it is your view.

Result
The participant has the facts on every option in a form they can use.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q16
Time limit
Within 5 business days of step 11 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 5POL-SCO-02 C5Written on: →Form, question 16Form Q16

Step 14

Coordinator

Ask the participant to tell you, in their own way, what each option is and what choosing it would mean.

Do not ask "Do you understand?". Write what they say, sign or show. If something is missing, explain it another way and ask again. If they still cannot, offer more time or a they choose. If it is still not clear, see "If it goes wrong".

Result
You know the participant understands, or you know what is still to explain.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q17
Time limit
In the same meeting as step 13 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 5POL-SCO-02 C5Written on: →Form, question 17Form Q17

Step 15

Coordinator

Tell the participant how long they have to decide, and leave the decision with them.

Say any real deadline, such as the plan end date or a provider's waiting list, and where it comes from. Say they can take time, talk to people they trust and ask for an advocate. If they want to wait, agree a date to ask again. Never say an offer will close unless it will.

Result
The participant decides at their own pace, knowing any real deadline.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q18
Time limit
At the end of the same meeting as step 14 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 6POL-SCO-02 C6Written on: →Form, question 18Form Q18

Decide

Step 16

Coordinator

Write down what the participant decided and exactly how they direct their funds.

Use their words for the decision and the purpose. Write the support, the provider, the funds to use, how much, the start and end dates, and any condition they set. If they have not decided, write "not decided", the date to ask again and any deadline. If they choose none of the options, write that, and go back to step 8 with what they said was missing. If they later change their mind, open a new copy and keep this one.

Result
The decision and the are on the record in the participant's terms.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q19 to Q20; REG-SCO-01 sheet 2 col C and col I
Time limit
On the day the participant decides (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 1POL-SCO-02 C1←POL-SCO-02, commitment 14POL-SCO-02 C14Written on: →Form, question 19Form Q19→Form, question 20Form Q20

Step 17

Coordinator

If the participant's choice carries a risk to them:

Explain the risk, and record what you said and what the participant chose.

Say the risk in plain words and what could reduce it. A risk alone is never a reason to refuse. If the risk is serious, complete FRM-RGT-04 Dignity of Risk Decision Record, follow PRO-RGT-04 Independence and Informed Choice Procedure, and tell the Service Manager.

Result
The participant chose with the risk in view, and their choice stands.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q21
Time limit
In the same meeting as step 16 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 6POL-SCO-02 C6Written on: →Form, question 21Form Q21

Step 18

Coordinator

If someone other than the participant makes the decision:

Ask the participant for their own wishes, and record them beside the decision.

Ask in their way of communicating, and alone if they want that. If their wishes differ from the decision, record both and tell the Service Manager the same day. The 's legal authority stands. Ask them to take the participant's wishes into account, and offer the participant an advocate.

Result
The participant's own voice is on the record.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q22
Time limit
In the same meeting as step 16 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 2POL-SCO-02 C2Written on: →Form, question 22Form Q22

Step 19

Coordinator

Read the record back to the participant and ask whether it says what they want.

Use their format. Change anything they say is wrong. Tell them they can change the record at any time. Tell them they can ask for a different coordinator or an independent advocate. Tell them they can complain to us or to the . Say how to do each. Ask them to confirm in the way they choose.

Result
The participant has confirmed the record and knows their rights.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q23 to Q24
Time limit
In the same meeting as step 16 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 6POL-SCO-02 C6←POL-SCO-02, commitment 14POL-SCO-02 C14Written on: →Form, question 23Form Q23→Form, question 24Form Q24

Arrange

Step 20

Warning. Taking, holding or paying out a participant's funds, or accepting a gift from a provider, puts the participant at risk and ends our independence.

Coordinator

Arrange the support exactly as the participant directed.

Contact the provider with the participant's consent and share only what the provider needs. Ask the provider to confirm the support, the price, the start date and who will deliver it. Make sure the provider can be paid from the funds the participant chose, in the way those funds are managed. Agree no change without the participant. Take, hold and pay out no funds, and accept no gift or benefit.

Result
The support is arranged as directed, and nothing passes through us.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q25
Time limit
Within 2 business days of step 19 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 1POL-SCO-02 C1←POL-SCO-02, commitment 3POL-SCO-02 C3Written on: →Form, question 25Form Q25

Step 21

Coordinator

Check with the participant that what was arranged matches their direction.

Compare the provider's confirmation with question 20, line by line. Tell the participant each difference and why. Change nothing until they agree. If it does not match and cannot be fixed, go back to step 16. Give them their copy of sections A to F, in their format.

Result
The participant has agreed that the arrangement is theirs.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q26; REG-SCO-01 sheet 2 col J
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the provider's confirmation (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 1POL-SCO-02 C1Written on: →Form, question 26Form Q26

Step 22

Coordinator

Help the participant make their own service agreement with the provider.

Explain what a service agreement is. It should cover the supports, the price, how to cancel or change it, and how to complain. Let the participant read it in their format. For NDIA-managed and plan-managed funds, check the prices against the NDIA price limit that applies; for self-managed funds, check the price is the one the participant agreed at question 14. Check the terms against question 20. The participant, or their decision maker, signs. Never sign for them. AGR-SUP-01 Service Agreement Template shows what a good agreement covers.

Result
The participant understands and has agreed the terms with the provider.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q27
Time limit
Before the first support is delivered (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 10POL-SCO-02 C10Written on: →Form, question 27Form Q27

Build skills

Step 23

Coordinator

Agree with the participant which skills they want to build, and how.

Go through each skill on question 28: coordinating supports, choosing and changing providers, managing funds and budget, directing workers, taking part in plan reviews, making service agreements, and using the flexibility in the plan. Ask what they do now and what they want to do alone. "Not now" is a valid answer. Record it, and ask again at each 3 monthly review. Never tie a support to whether they want to learn.

Result
A in the participant's words exists, or their choice not to have one is recorded.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q28 to Q29; REG-SCO-01 sheet 2 col K
Time limit
Within 20 business days of the first record, then at each 3 monthly review (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 8POL-SCO-02 C8Written on: →Form, question 28Form Q28→Form, question 29Form Q29

Step 24

Coordinator

Explain how NDIA planning works and the participant's part in it.

Cover how a plan review works and what the participant brings. Cover how to ask for a change, how service agreements work, and how funds can move within the plan. Use their format and ask them to say it back. Add what you gave to REG-RGT-01 Communication and Accessible Information Register.

Result
The participant understands how to take part in NDIA planning.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q30
Time limit
Within 20 business days of the first record, and again at step 30 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 9POL-SCO-02 C9Written on: →Form, question 30Form Q30

Step 25

Coordinator

Review the participant's skills plan with them.

Ask what they now do on their own. Hand over one more task if they want it. Step back where they can manage. Agree the date of the next review.

Result
The skills plan is up to date, and you have stepped back as far as the participant wants.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q31
Time limit
Every 3 months from the first record (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 8POL-SCO-02 C8Written on: →Form, question 31Form Q31

Keep watch

Step 26

Coordinator

Check each category of the participant's funds against what was planned.

This is the one monthly funds check, set in PRO-SCO-02 step 22 and recorded on FRM-SCO-02 Section H; do not run a second one. Use the participant's statement, the plan manager's statement or the NDIA portal, with consent. For each category, compare the share of the plan amount used and booked with the share of the plan time that has passed, and write the forecast at plan end. Mark any gap over 15 percentage points. Show the participant what you found, and tell them within 5 business days.

Result
You and the participant both know where the funds stand.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q32 to Q34; REG-SCO-01 col AF; REG-SCO-01 sheet 2 col L
Time limit
In the first 5 business days of each month (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 11POL-SCO-02 C11Written on: →Form, question 32Form Q32→Form, question 33Form Q33→Form, question 34Form Q34

Step 27

Coordinator

If a category is off track, or will run out before the plan ends:

Work out why, and agree with the participant what to do.

Use Decision table 3. Ask the provider and the participant what caused it. Offer the options and let the participant choose. Tell the Service Manager the same day if funds will run out more than 30 days before the plan ends.

Result
The participant has chosen what to do, and the Service Manager knows of any early run out.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q35
Time limit
Within 5 business days of step 26 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 11POL-SCO-02 C11Written on: →Form, question 35Form Q35

Step 28

Coordinator

Check with the participant whether each funded support is helping them reach their goal.

Ask the participant first, in their way. Then look at hours delivered against hours planned, cancellations, progress against the goal, and any concern or complaint. If a support is not helping, offer to change or end it. If they agree, go back to step 8 for a new option, or end it as they direct. When a support changes or ends, check that FRM-SCO-01 still names who acts if it breaks down.

Result
Each support is kept, changed or ended on the participant's decision.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q36; REG-SCO-01 sheet 2 col M
Time limit
Every 3 months, or within 10 business days of the participant saying a support is not working (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 12POL-SCO-02 C12Written on: →Form, question 36Form Q36

Step 29

Coordinator

Link the participant with the mainstream, community and informal supports they chose.

For each need, ask which they want to try, such as health, education, transport, housing, work, local groups, family and friends. With consent, make the introduction, go with them if they ask, and follow up. Write what is in the way. If a refuses or has a long wait, offer an advocate and tell the Service Manager.

Result
The participant is connected to the supports they chose, and barriers are known.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q37
Time limit
Within 10 business days of the participant agreeing (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 13POL-SCO-02 C13Written on: →Form, question 37Form Q37

Step 30

Coordinator

Prepare the participant for their plan review.

Follow PRO-SCO-02 step 23, which sets the one plan review preparation: start 12 weeks before the plan reassessment date; give the participant their plain summary of how funds were used, what worked and what did not, with the draft report, at least 8 weeks before it; the report goes 6 weeks before it, or by the NDIA's date (PRO-SCO-02 step 24). Ask what they want in the next plan and write it in their words. Offer to go with them. The participant decides what to ask for. Repeat step 24.

Result
The participant goes into the plan review prepared, and in charge of what they ask for.
Record
FRM-SCO-02 Q38; REG-SCO-01 sheet 2 col N
Time limit
Start 12 weeks before the plan reassessment date (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SCO-02, commitment 9POL-SCO-02 C9Written on: →Form, question 38Form Q38

6Decision

Decision table 1: who decides (step 1).

IfThen
The participant is an adult and no legal document says otherwiseThe participant decides. Ask every question of them yourself
The participant has a supporter they choseThe participant decides, with the supporter's help. The supporter never decides for them
A guardian, nominee or other person holds legal authority that covers this decisionThat person decides. Record what the document covers. Ask the participant for their own wishes (step 18)
The participant is a childThe person with parental responsibility decides. Ask the child for their views in a way that suits them, and record them
The document is missing, out of date or does not cover this decisionAct on no one's direction yet. Tell the Service Manager. Ask the participant, in their way, what they want

Decision table 2: can it be arranged (step 6).

IfThen
The support is in the plan, the funds are enough, and it is safe and lawfulArrange it as directed
The choice carries a risk to the participant onlyArrange it. Record the risk talk (step 17)
The plan does not clearly cover the supportAsk the NDIA, with consent. Tell the participant what you asked and what the answer was
The funds are not enoughTell the participant (step 7). Offer a cheaper option, a mainstream support, or a request to change the plan
The provider is not registered and the funds are NDIA-managedThat provider cannot be paid. Offer others (step 9)
The support is unlawful, or would seriously harm another personDo not arrange it. Tell the participant (step 7). Tell the Service Manager the same day

Decision table 3: funds check result (step 27). The gap is in percentage points between the share of the plan amount used and booked and the share of plan time passed (PRO-SCO-02 step 22).

IfThen
Used and booked is within 15 percentage points of the share of plan time passedNo action. Tell the participant at the next meeting
Used and booked is more than 15 percentage points behindAsk why: a support not delivered, cancellations, a provider's wait, or the participant's choice. Offer to fix it
Used and booked is more than 15 percentage points aheadForecast to plan end. Ask what changed: extra hours, a price change or a one-off cost. Offer options
Funds will run out more than 30 days before the plan endsTell the Service Manager the same day. Offer options: fewer hours, moving funds if the plan allows, or a request to change the plan
A category is empty and a support still needs itTell the participant and the provider the same day, and tell the Service Manager. Do not let the support stop without the participant knowing

7If it goes wrong

  • The participant does not want to answer, or does not want to decide. Record what they said and stop. Do not push. Agree a date to ask again. Tell the Service Manager if a plan end date or a provider's wait falls within 20 business days. Never decide for them.
  • You cannot understand the participant, or the communication support cannot be booked in time. Do not carry on with a guess, or with a family member standing in. Move the meeting and tell the participant why. Tell the Service Manager the same day. Offer an independent advocate.
  • You cannot tell what the participant wants. Spend time with them, and with people who know them well if they agree. Watch what they choose. Record their wishes as you understand them and how you know. Tell the Service Manager. POL-RGT-03 Independence and Informed Choice Policy covers supported decision-making.
  • A family member, provider or plan manager pushes a choice that is not the participant's. Follow the participant's wishes. Tell the Service Manager. Offer an advocate. If you think the participant is being harmed or exploited, follow PRO-SGD-01 Violence, Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination Procedure the same day.
  • The participant changes their mind, or a support stops working. Open a new copy of FRM-SCO-02 and start at step 5. Keep the old copy. Tell the provider only what the participant agrees. Check that FRM-SCO-01 Risk and Crisis Response Plan still names who acts if the support breaks down.
  • The participant wants to change how their funds are managed, for example to self-manage. Explain what each way involves, and what they would take on. Help them ask the NDIA, which decides. Record their wish in question 30.
  • The participant will not share their funds figures, or you cannot see them. Record it. Work from what they tell you, and say on the record that the funds check is limited. Ask again at the next funds check.
  • The participant will lose a within 20 business days, or the need is marked urgent (PRO-SCO-02 step 15; PRO-SCO-01 Decision table 3). Tell the Service Manager the same day. Use the urgent path under Before you start: steps 5 to 20 within 3 business days, by phone where needed, with the record completed within 2 business days afterwards. POL-COS-01 Continuity of Supports Policy applies.
  • The funds check shows claims for supports the participant says were not delivered, or the participant was pressured to accept a support. Tell the Service Manager the same day. Do not confront the provider. The Chief Executive decides within 2 business days whether to report to the NDIA fraud reporting line and the NDIS Commission, and whether PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure applies. Record it on FRM-SCO-02 questions 34 and 35 and as an event in REG-SCO-01 column AE.
  • You are away, or you will miss a deadline. Tell the Service Manager before the deadline passes. The Service Manager confirms the cover coordinator named under PRO-SCO-02 step 1 within 1 business day and tells the participant who it is. The cover coordinator reads the file and carries on from the last finished step. Write the reason for the delay in the participant's file. A sole trader's cover coordinator is the coordinator from another provider named on adoption, and PRO-COS-01 Continuity of Supports Procedure covers the participant's supports if they cannot work.
  • A provider or participant offers you a gift or benefit. Decline it. Record the offer on FRM-GOV-01 Conflict of Interest Declaration Form the same day.
  • You think a colleague is steering participants towards a provider, or taking gifts. Tell the Chief Executive. If the concern is about the Chief Executive or the owner, tell the chair of the governing body or the independent contact for concerns. POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy protects you.
  • The participant is unhappy with our advice, or with you. Tell them they can ask for a different coordinator and how to complain. PRO-FBK-01 sets how a complaint is handled.
  • You shared information the participant had not agreed to share. Tell the Service Manager the same day. Treat it as an incident under PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure.
  • A record is wrong. Add a new entry with the date and the reason. Never overwrite or delete the old one.
  • The participant is leaving us. Follow PRO-SUP-04 Transitions to or from a Provider Procedure. Give them a copy of the records they ask for. Hand over to a new coordinator only with their consent.

8Done means

  • Each decision has a FRM-SCO-02 with every needed answer in questions 1 to 27, confirmed by the participant (question 24), and filed.
  • What was arranged matches what the participant directed (question 26), and a service agreement is in place (question 27).
  • REG-SCO-01 Support Coordination Register sheet 2 holds a row for each decision, funds check and review, and sheet 1 columns Z and AF show the dates.
  • A skills plan exists, or the participant's choice not to have one is recorded (questions 28 and 29). It is reviewed every 3 months (question 31).
  • A funds check (questions 32 to 34) exists for every month, and a support review (questions 36 and 37) for every 3 months.
  • From 12 weeks before the plan reassessment date, the participant has their summary for the plan review (question 38).

9Quick card

118 words
  • Ask the participant first, and find out who decides. (step 1)
  • Meet in their way of communicating. Book support before you meet. (step 2)
  • Write what they want in their words before you suggest anything. (step 5)
  • Find at least three suitable options, at least two with no relationship to us, and list mainstream and community supports as well. (step 8)
  • Ask them to say it back. Never ask "Do you understand?". (step 14)
  • Never choose for them. Tell them any real deadline. (step 15)
  • Arrange only what they directed, then check it matches. (step 20)
  • Never hold their money. Never take a gift. (step 20)
  • Check the funds every month, once, on FRM-SCO-02 Section H. (step 26)

form.intro:
Use this record to show how a participant chose a support and how we explained their options. It also shows how their funds are used and watched, and what they are learning to do for themself. The coordinator completes it with the participant, and writes the participant's words, not their own.

Use a new copy each time, and give each copy its own record number. This form holds four uses in one; the list below gives the minimum questions for each use (a split into separate forms is planned for 0.4.0):

  • When: a decision about a support (Sections A to F). Complete these questions: 1 to 27, with 10, 21 and 22 only where they apply. One copy may cover several supports arranged together for the same purpose; name each support at question 20.
  • When: the (Section G). Complete these questions: on the copy for the participant's first decision, 1 and 28 to 30; at each 3 monthly review, 1, 28, 29 and 31 on the review copy; question 30 again when you prepare the plan review.
  • When: the monthly funds check (Section H), a new copy every month in the first 5 business days of the month. Complete these questions: 1 and 32 to 35. This is the one monthly funds check for the participant (PRO-SCO-02 step 22).
  • When: the support review and plan review preparation (Section I). Complete these questions: at each 3 monthly review, 1, 36 and 37; from 12 weeks before the plan reassessment date, 1 and 38.

Answer question 1 on every copy. File every copy for a participant together, newest last.

Have ready:

  • the participant's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form
  • their consent in FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form
  • their plan or latest statement, if they choose to share it.

Ask the participant themself first. Ask a family member or other only when the participant wants that, or when that person holds legal authority to decide.

What happens next: the coordinator enters each copy as a row in REG-SCO-01 Support Coordination Register sheet 2 and gives the participant their copy. PRO-SCO-03 Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure sets every step.

Short names used in the question protocol:

  • "The Practice Standards Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018.
  • "The Code Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018.
form.privacy:
We collect this information to help you choose supports, to arrange them as you direct and to watch your funds with you. We also collect it to meet our duties under the NDIS Act 2013 and the NDIS Practice Standards.

Your coordinator and the Service Manager read it. The Quality Manager reads samples to check our work. We share it with a provider, a service or a person only as you agree in FRM-INF-01, or where a law requires or allows it. We never share it to push you towards a choice.

You can choose not to answer a question. Tell us, and we will explain what that means for the help we can give.

You can ask to see what we hold and ask us to correct it. We keep this record for 7 years after your coordination with us ends, or longer where the NDIS Act 2013 (section 45B) or the law of [state or territory] requires, and until you turn 25 if you were under 18. We use it only for your supports. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect it.
form.after:
• Coordinator: file the copy in the participant's file and enter it as a row in REG-SCO-01 sheet 2 within 2 business days (our standard).
  • Coordinator: give the participant their copy of Sections A to F, in their format, when you do step 21 of PRO-SCO-03 (our standard). Give a copy of any later section when they ask.
  • Coordinator: tell the Service Manager the same day if any of these is true (our standard):
    • question 9 is "no"
    • question 15 is "yes"
    • question 21 shows a serious risk
    • question 22 shows the wishes differ
    • question 34 shows funds will run out early.
  • Service Manager: read REG-SCO-01 every month for overdue funds checks and plan reassessment dates within 12 weeks (our standard).
  • Quality Manager: sample five completed records, or all of them if there are fewer than five, every 3 months (our standard).
  • If the record is about a participant close to the coordinator, the Service Manager gives it to another coordinator. For a sole trader, the reads it.
  • Keep each record for 7 years after the participant's coordination row in REG-SCO-01 closes (our standard), or longer where section 45B of the NDIS Act 2013 or the law of [state or territory] requires, and until the participant turns 25 where they were under 18. Never overwrite an answer. Add a new dated entry with the reason.

register.proves:
This register is the running record of at [Provider name]. Sheet 1 holds one row for each for each period. A row shows the participant's risks, their plan, the engaged, what we checked and what we reported, and when. Sheet 2 holds one row for each FRM-SCO-02 Support and Choice Record: each decision about a support, , monthly , support review and plan review preparation.

Short names used here:

  • "The Registration Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018.
  • "The Incident Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.
  • "The Code" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018, section 6.
  • "The " means the National Disability Insurance Agency. The Quality Indicators call it "the Agency".

What it evidences, and how long it is kept:

  • Indicators evidenced: s 64 (1) to s 64 (6), on sheet 1. Sheet 2 holds the record for s 65 (1) to s 65 (4). FRM-SCO-02 Support Options and Choice Record and PRO-SCO-03 Management of a Participant's NDIS Supports Procedure feed sheet 2.
  • Legal basis: Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 6, clause 3, and Quality Indicators Guidelines, section 64. The Rules do not set the columns of this register. The columns are our standard, built from the six indicators.
  • Records that are kept elsewhere stay there. An incident is recorded in REG-INC-01 Incident Register, and a complaint in REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register. This register holds the number of each, in column AM.
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years after the row is closed (our standard), and in every case for the 7 years that section 45B of the NDIS Act 2013 (from 27 August 2026) requires for records of claims and supports. For a participant who was under 18 when coordination started, keep it until they turn 25, when that is later (our standard).
  • Other law can require longer. Check the law of [state or territory] before any row is destroyed. Never destroy a row while a claim, an inquiry, a complaint or an investigation is open.

Every column is filled for every row, except where the Required column says otherwise.
register.entry:
1. The opens the row within 1 of the participant agreeing to start (our standard). When the coordinator is away, the or the Service Manager opens it.
  2. Keep one open row for each participant. When a new NDIS plan starts, the coordinator closes the old row with the reason "plan period ended and a new row opened" and opens a new one within 10 business days of learning the new plan dates (our standard). Column AM links the two rows. The plan and risk level carry over by copy and are then reviewed. No handover is needed for this kind of closing.
  3. Add each entry on the day it happens, or within 1 business day (our standard). Where a column holds more than one entry, each entry is a dated line with the name of the person who made it. A new line never replaces an old one.
  4. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason. Where the register is a workbook, keep version history switched on.
  5. For a crisis, write the time we learned of it and the time of our first response in column AE. The two times show whether we met the 2 hour standard.
  6. Long text stays in the form. Where a column says "one dated line each", the lines live on a child sheet keyed by column A (see Rows), and the participant's row shows the latest date and the next due date. In a workbook, write one line and the question number, for example "see FRM-SCO-01 Q12". Never copy a participant's full account into a cell.
  7. Column K is filled at the first meeting. Columns O, Q and S are filled inside the time in PRO-SCO-02 Decision table 2. For a participant at high or extreme risk, columns K, Q and S are filled before any provider is briefed.
  8. When systems are down, write the entry on paper and enter it within 1 business day of the system coming back.
  9. When a row is about a concern with a coordinator, the Service Manager restricts who can see it. When the concern is about the Service Manager, the Chief Executive does. In a provider with one owner, the does.
  10. Reopen a closed row when new information arrives. Set column AJ to "open" and record the reason in column AM.

A row is closed only when all of these are true:

  • the reason for closing is recorded in column AK
  • every report in column AG up to the closing date is sent, or the reason it was not sent is in column AH
  • every event in column AE has a plan review date
  • the plan was handed over, or the participant's refusal of handover is recorded in column AL; or the reason in column AK is "plan period ended and a new row opened" and column AM links the rows, in which case no handover is needed
  • the participant has their copy of the current plan, recorded in column S
  • the Service Manager has approved the closing. For a participant who was at high or extreme risk, the has also read the row.

register.see:
• The coordinator and the cover coordinator can see their participants' rows.
  • The Service Manager, the Quality Manager and the Chief Executive can see every row.
  • The case reviewer can see the rows they review.
  • A participant can ask to see their own row. We remove other people's details first.
  • A provider cannot see this register. A provider sees only the parts of the plan the participant agreed to share (column N).

Rows hold sensitive personal and health information, and sometimes information about people at risk from someone close to them. Keep the register in [system name], with a login for each person and a log of changes. Lock away any paper record. Never leave one in a participant's home or in a car.
